summary: Investigation of alert HHF-002 on card C06220-K1 identified an undocumented, syndicated card-not-present fraud scheme. Between January 17 and January 19, 2017, the card was subjected to three unauthorized online product-C charges totaling $2,166.71 (transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127). Each transaction utilized a different newly introduced device (D009715, D009718, and D009721) operating behind anonymous proxies, matching identical attack patterns seen on peer cards C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1. The activity was confirmed as fraud with a probability of 0.93, resulting in card blocking, case escalation, regulatory reporting under Policy R9, and monitoring of connected accounts.
open_question: While the cross-card attack signature and anonymous proxy rotation establish a syndicated fraud campaign, direct cardholder outreach to confirm non-recognition of transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127 would confirm the compromise vector and establish exact monetary loss.

waiting.why: R9 and 3a: coordinated abuse that fits no documented pattern
